pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

2. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. newton (N)

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

7. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

8. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

9. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Primary consumers only

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

2. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

4. D — newton (N)

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

6. D — Ice melting to water

7. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

8. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

9. A — Producers

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

11. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reproduction in plants; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Curved mirrors; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Structure of the atom; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
